deities: Goddess Chhinnamasta (one of the Ten Mahavidyas)

history.summary: TOWN CORRECTED: CSV says Muzaffarpur, but the famous Chhinmastika temple is at Kanti (~15 km from the city), on NH-28 — town corrected to Kanti. A Shakta shrine dedicated to Goddess Chhinnamasta, one of the Ten Mahavidyas; the goddess is depicted holding a sword in her right hand and her own severed head in her left, symbolising self-sacrifice and transcendence. Described by online vloggers as the second Chhinmastika temple in the country and the only one in Bihar — UNVERIFIED by authoritative sources. It draws devotees year-round and heavy crowds during Navratri, including tantric practitioners. NOTE: a smaller, separate Chhinmastika Mandir exists at Saraiyaganj, Tilak Nagar in Muzaffarpur city; do not conflate the two.

name: Chhinmastika Mandir
town_description: Kanti is a town in Muzaffarpur district, Bihar, about 15 km west of Muzaffarpur city on NH-28. It is best known as an industrial centre, home to the Kanti Thermal Power Station (George Fernandes Thermal Power Station) and NTPC facilities. The town serves as a small commercial and transit hub for the surrounding agricultural belt of north Bihar, and is growing as a residential spillover of Muzaffarpur city.
